 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Close this content Michael Jackson’s Brother Reveals He’s Had Cancer for 4 Years and It’s Now Stage 4
 In Touch Weekly Follow Clara Awuse Add to Preferred Sources Updated Thu, November 19, 2026 at 6:26 PM UTC PNP/ WENN.com Marlon Jackson has been quietly battling cancer for years.
 The Jackson 5 member, 69, revealed he has been living with prostate cancer for the past four years during an appearance on The Farah Shammas Podcast , TMZ reported on Thursday, November 19. According to the outlet, his cancer is currently stage 4.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "I've had cancer for four years," Marlon said on the podcast.
 Despite the diagnosis, the singer insisted he's in good spirits. "I'm great. I'm good. Bad grass don't die. So, I'm going to be around for a long time," he assured.
 Marlon explained that he has already undergone major treatment. "I've had my prostate gland removed, and I've had radiation treatment, and everything is fine. Everything is great," he shared.
 The "ABC" singer also opened up about the lifestyle changes he's made since his diagnosis, including staying active. "I walk almost four miles four times a week. You know, and that's great for me," he said.
 Advertisement Advertisement Marlon added that he has cut sugar from his diet and is "careful what I put in my body and try to take care of myself." He said his doctor even told him, "You're doing so much better than what I thought." Until now, Marlon had kept his diagnosis private.
 Marlon rose to fame alongside his brothers Jackie , Tito , Jermaine and Michael Jackson as part of the Jackson 5, the Motown group behind hits including "I Want You Back," "ABC" and "I'll Be There." The group was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1997. 
 His vow to "be around for a long time" carries extra weight for the Jackson family, which has already endured painful losses. Tito died in September 2024 at age 70, and Michael died in 2009 at age 50. Now, Marlon says he's focused on taking care of himself so he can stay healthy for years to come.
